title: Geo-staggered binding and degrade-variant orchestration
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: When performing staged model version rollouts (canary / A-B) we observe unsafe cross-region spills and elevated tail latencies when regional capacity saturates. Current pinning semantics anchor sessions to a variant without accounting for multi-tier headroom or variant degrade paths, which can cause cascading evictions and poor user experience.

Goal: Design and implement a routing policy called 'geo-staggered binding' that supports: cohort-scoped pinning windows, region adjacency awareness to avoid cross-region fallback storms, tier-aware headroom budgeting, and an explicit 'degrade-variant orchestration' mechanism that selects fallback variants based on an ordered safety matrix (latency budget, cost multiplier, model-compatibility score). The system should gracefully release pins (probabilistic decay) and allow canary cohorts to graduate or be drained without destabilizing regional capacity.
decisions: 1) Introduce a cohort-scoped binding TTL and a probabilistic release mechanism instead of indefinite session pins. 2) Fallback selection will be policy-driven using an ordered safety matrix (primary: latency within regional budget, secondary: cost multiplier threshold, tertiary: semantic-compatibility tag). 3) Region adjacency rules will prefer intra-region fallbacks, then geo-adjacent tiers, only falling back cross-continent as last resort. 4) Implement soft headroom reservations per tier for canary cohorts to avoid eviction cascades.
tradeoffs:
- Stronger safety matrix and adjacency checks reduce the chance of cross-region spikes, but add routing decision CPU and increase config surface area.
- Probabilistic pin release smooths traffic but can slightly reduce deterministic session affinity for long-lived sessions.
- Tier headroom reservation improves stability at the cost of temporarily lower utilization during rollouts.
implementation_steps: 1) Extend routing-policy proto with fields: cohort_id, binding_ttl_ms, release_probability, safety_matrix_ref, adjacency_policy_ref.
2) Implement decision engine module that evaluates (region_capacity, tier_headroom, p99_latency_estimate, safety_matrix) and emits route with an action tag (PIN / PIN_DEFER / FALLBACK_TO_VARIANT).
3) Update session-store to record cohort binding metadata and probabilistic-release counters; add TTL eviction worker with exponential backoff on retries.
4) Add tier-headroom budgeting controller: reserve ephemeral capacity slices for active canary cohorts and expose metrics for reserved_vs_available.
5) Implement degrade-variant orchestrator: given a set of compatible variants, rank them by safety_matrix and generate fallback chain with explicit reason codes.
6) Wire observability: dashboards for cohort heatmaps, headroom pressure, fallback waterfall (counts by reason), and p99/p999 tail-latency per-variant.
7) Create an operator CLI to force-coerce cohort graduation, immediate pin release, or emergency drain.
8) Add integration tests and chaos tests that simulate regional GPU exhaustion and validate degrade behavior.
9) Roll out in canary: start with internal-only cohorts, then opt-in beta customers, then global rollout with staggered cohort enable flags.
10) Post-deploy review and telemetry-driven tuning (safety matrix thresholds, release_probability defaults).
test_plan: Unit tests for routing decision engine with synthetic capacity/latency inputs
Integration tests across two-region testbed (us-west1, eu-west1) validating adjacency rules
Load test: create sustained canary cohort at 30% of tier headroom and validate no cross-region spill for 90m
Chaos test: randomly kill 30% of GPUs in a region and ensure degrade chain keeps request success rate >= 99% and p99 latency within SLO for fallback tier
End-to-end tests: session affinity observed for 95% of requests within cohort binding TTL
Regression tests: pin-release does not introduce loops or request oscillation across variants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit and integration tests, feature flag gated behind routing.orchestrator.v2
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal teams and 2 low-impact customers; monitor headroom and fallback rates for 72h
Phase 2 (beta): expand to 20% of traffic for teams with non-critical workloads, tune safety_matrix thresholds
Phase 3 (ga): enable by default for new rollouts, provide opt-out knob for legacy pinning semantics for 30 days
Emergency: operator CLI to immediately revert cohorts to legacy pin behavior and drain canary reservations
monitoring: Alert: fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 10m AND headroom_available < 10%
comments: 2026-02-26 - Priya Patel: Initial proposal drafted after incident where canary in eu-west spilled into us-west causing doubled egress e2e latencies. See incident notes and rough spec.

2026-03-02 - Marco Silva (review): +1 on adjacency rules; we should add an explicit per-tenant threshold to avoid multi-tenant noisy neighbor issues. Also suggest default release_probability=0.02 for 5m windows.
2026-03-05 - Design feedback (Lina Gomez): We need a simple visualization in Console that clearly shows cohort pin state and fallback chain to reduce operator cognitive load.
2026-03-08 - Security (Anika Bose): No new secrets expected; confirm KMS usage not required. Marked security_review_required=false.
2026-03-10 - Ethan Chen: Implemented proto extension and decision-engine skeleton; pushing draft PR for early feedback. Performance microbenchmark attached in PR.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing decision engine applied to testbed chooses intra-region fallbacks preferentially and only uses cross-continent fallback as last resort.
2) Canary cohorts with reserved headroom do not trigger region-wide evictions in load tests.
3) Pin release mechanism reduces pinned sessions by >= 40% in 1h for churn-heavy workloads.
4) Observability dashboards show fallback rates and headroom metrics with <15s ingest latency.
5) No regressions in core throughput or p95 latency for non-canary traffic in 1-week canary window.
notes:
- Safety matrix is intentionally pluggable: initial matrix will be simple numeric thresholds but later can be ML-scored compatibility.
- This ticket intentionally avoids touching client SDKs; server-side behavior only.
- Follow-on work: expose cohort controls in Console and add tenant-scoped override policies.
